slides.text: The local coffee shop had a strictly enforced 'take an umbrella, leave an umbrella' bin by the door. It was Seattle; it rained constantly. One morning, I accidentally left my absolute favorite yellow umbrella in the bin. The next day, it was gone, replaced by a sleek black one. Inside the black umbrella, a handwritten note was taped to the handle: 'Sorry I took the yellow one. It brightened my gloomy day.'

I smiled, wrote a note back, taped it inside, and left the black umbrella in the bin. 'Keep the yellow one. Sounds like you need the sunshine.' For three months, we actively traded umbrellas and secrets. He was an architect struggling with burnout; I was a cellist with crippling stage fright. We fell entirely in love on tiny squares of paper, dodging the rain, never actually knowing each other's faces.

One torrential Tuesday, I rushed into the café. The bin was completely empty. Defeated, I turned to leave, but a tall, handsome man in a soaking wet trench coat stood blocking the door. He was holding my bright yellow umbrella over his shoulder. He looked at my stunned face, smiled nervously, and held it out to me. 'I think it's finally time we shared the sunshine together.'
